FILE: .gitea/workflows/ci.yml
name: Sport Analytics CI

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  plan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 5
    outputs:
      full: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.full }}
      evidence: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.evidence }}
      docs: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.docs }}
      frontend: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.frontend }}
      lighthouse: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.lighthouse }}
      backend: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.backend }}
      worker: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.worker }}
      contracts: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.contracts }}
      database: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.database }}
      e2e: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.e2e }}
      e2eFull: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.e2eFull }}
      intermediateIngestion: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.intermediateIngestion }}
      hygiene: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.hygiene }}
      deployment: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.deployment }}
      openapi: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.openapi }}
      apiContract: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.apiContract }}
      coverage: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.coverage }}
      deployFrontend: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.deployFrontend }}
      deployBackend: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.deployBackend }}
      deployWorker: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.deployWorker }}
      deployDocs: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.deployDocs }}
      needsNpm: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.needsNpm }}

    steps:
      - name: Check out repository history
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22

      - name: Check required repository structure
        run: node scripts/check-required-files.mjs

      - name: Plan change-aware validation
        id: plan
        env:
          CI_EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
          CI_PR_BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          CI_PUSH_BEFORE_SHA: ${{ github.event.before }}
          CI_HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: node scripts/ci-change-plan.mjs

      - name: Check committed patch whitespace
        env:
          CI_EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
          CI_PR_BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          CI_PUSH_BEFORE_SHA: ${{ github.event.before }}
          CI_HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          if [ "$CI_EVENT_NAME" = "pull_request" ]; then
            base="$CI_PR_BASE_SHA"
          else
            base="$CI_PUSH_BEFORE_SHA"
          fi

          if [ -z "$base" ] || printf '%s' "$base" | grep -Eq '^0+$'; then
            base="$(git rev-parse "${CI_HEAD_SHA}^")"
          fi

          git diff --check "${base}...${CI_HEAD_SHA}" -- . ':(exclude)evidence/ai/transcripts/**'

      - name: Validate frozen dependency lockfile
        if: steps.plan.outputs.needsNpm == 'true'
        run: npm ci --dry-run --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund

      - name: Test CI change-routing rules
        run: node --test tests/ci/*.test.mjs

  validation:
    needs: plan
    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'push' &&
      needs.plan.outputs.needsNpm == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 25
    env:
      NODE_ENV: test
      KNIP_DISABLE_RAW_TRANSFER: '1'
      SUPABASE_URL: https://example.invalid
      SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY: test-publishable-key

    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: package-lock.json

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      # These node tests guard the natural-language evaluation set, which is run by
      # hand against a paid provider â€” a case that silently stops testing anything
      # is only ever discovered by paying for a run. They need the installed
      # dependencies, so they run here rather than in the plan job. Any change under
      # scripts/ selects a full plan, so the needsNpm gate never skips them for a
      # change they could catch.
      - name: Test repository script modules
        if: needs.plan.outputs.needsNpm == 'true'
        run: npm run test:scripts

      - name: Check repository formatting
        run: npm run format:check

      - name: Run monorepo architecture and hygiene checks
        if: needs.plan.outputs.hygiene == 'true'
        run: npm run hygiene

      - name: Verify shared contracts
        if: needs.plan.outputs.contracts == 'true'
        run: |
          npm run lint --workspace=@sport-analytics/contracts
          npm run typecheck --workspace=@sport-analytics/contracts
          npm run test:contracts
          npm run build --workspace=@sport-analytics/contracts

      - name: Verify backend workspace
        if: needs.plan.outputs.backend == 'true'
        run: |
          npm run lint --workspace=@sport-analytics/backend
          npm run typecheck --workspace=@sport-analytics/backend
          npm run test:unit
          npm run test:api
          npm run build --workspace=@sport-analytics/backend

      - name: Verify asynchronous worker workspace
        if: needs.plan.outputs.worker == 'true'
        run: |
          npm run lint --workspace=@sport-analytics/worker
          npm run typecheck --workspace=@sport-analytics/worker
          npm run test:worker
          npm run build --workspace=@sport-analytics/worker

      - name: Verify frontend workspace
        if: needs.plan.outputs.frontend == 'true'
        run: |
          npm run lint --workspace=@sport-analytics/frontend
          npm run typecheck --workspace=@sport-analytics/frontend
          npm run test:frontend -- -- --maxWorkers=2

      - name: Run PostgreSQL database integration tests
        if: needs.plan.outputs.database == 'true'
        run: npm run test:database

      - name: Run deployment-helper tests
        if: needs.plan.outputs.deployment == 'true'
        run: npm run test:deployment

      - name: Lint OpenAPI description
        if: needs.plan.outputs.openapi == 'true'
        run: npm run openapi:lint

      - name: Verify the API implementation against the OpenAPI contract
        if: needs.plan.outputs.apiContract == 'true'
        run: |
          npm run prepare:contracts --workspace=@sport-analytics/backend
          npm run test:api-contract

      - name: Verify Intermediate ingestion acceptance invariants
        if: needs.plan.outputs.intermediateIngestion == 'true'
        run: npm run verify:intermediate-ingestion:invariants

      - name: Set up Python
        if: needs.plan.outputs.docs == 'true'
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'
          cache: pip
          cache-dependency-path: requirements-docs.txt

      - name: Install documentation dependencies
        if: needs.plan.outputs.docs == 'true'
        run: python -m pip install -r requirements-docs.txt

      - name: Build documentation strictly
        if: needs.plan.outputs.docs == 'true'
        run: python -m mkdocs build --strict

  browser:
    needs: plan
    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'push' &&
      needs.plan.outputs.e2e == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 20
    env:
      PLAYWRIGHT_REUSE_BUILD: '1'
      PLAYWRIGHT_WORKERS: '2'
      VITE_SUPABASE_URL: https://e2e.supabase.co
      VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY: e2e-public-key

    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: package-lock.json

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Build shared contracts for browser validation
        run: npm run build --workspace=@sport-analytics/contracts

      - name: Build frontend production bundle once
        env:
          NODE_ENV: production
        run: npm run build --workspace=@sport-analytics/frontend

      - name: Restore Playwright Chromium cache
        id: playwright-cache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/ms-playwright
          key: playwright-ubuntu24-chromium-1.62.1

      - name: Ensure Playwright Chromium system dependencies
        run: npx playwright install-deps chromium

      - name: Install Playwright Chromium on cache miss
        if: steps.playwright-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: npx playwright install chromium

      - name: Run Intermediate ingestion browser acceptance
        if: >-
          needs.plan.outputs.intermediateIngestion == 'true' &&
          needs.plan.outputs.e2eFull != 'true'
        env:
          NODE_ENV: production
        run: >-
          npm run test:e2e --
          tests/e2e/submissions.spec.ts
          tests/e2e/batch-review-workspace.spec.ts
          tests/e2e/corrections.spec.ts

      - name: Confirm full browser suite covers Intermediate ingestion acceptance
        if: >-
          needs.plan.outputs.intermediateIngestion == 'true' &&
          needs.plan.outputs.e2eFull == 'true'
        run: echo "Full browser validation includes the submission, batch-review and correction acceptance journeys."

      - name: Run browser and accessibility tests
        if: needs.plan.outputs.e2eFull == 'true'
        env:
          NODE_ENV: production
        run: npm run test:e2e

  lighthouse:
    needs: plan
    if: >-
      needs.plan.outputs.lighthouse == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 30
    env:
      LIGHTHOUSE_RUNS: '3'
      LIGHTHOUSE_GATE_MODE: baseline
      LIGHTHOUSE_OUTPUT_DIR: artifacts/lighthouse-ci
      LIGHTHOUSE_ROUTES: /,/api,/competitions,/seasons,/fixtures,/competitors,/participants,/dataset-releases,/sign-in
      VITE_SUPABASE_URL: https://e2e.supabase.co
      VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY: e2e-public-key

    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: package-lock.json

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Build production frontend for Lighthouse
        run: |
          npm run build --workspace=@sport-analytics/contracts
          npm run build --workspace=@sport-analytics/frontend

      - name: Restore Playwright Chromium cache
        id: lighthouse-playwright-cache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/ms-playwright
          key: playwright-ubuntu24-chromium-1.62.1

      - name: Ensure Playwright Chromium system dependencies
        run: npx playwright install-deps chromium

      - name: Install Playwright Chromium on cache miss
        if: steps.lighthouse-playwright-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: npx playwright install chromium

      - name: Run Lighthouse production-preview baseline
        shell: bash
        run: |
          npm run preview --workspace=@sport-analytics/frontend -- --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4173 &
          preview_pid=$!
          trap 'kill "$preview_pid" 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT
          for attempt in $(seq 1 30); do
            if curl --fail --silent http://127.0.0.1:4173/ >/dev/null; then
              break
            fi
            sleep 1
          done
          curl --fail --silent http://127.0.0.1:4173/ >/dev/null
          export CHROME_PATH="$(node -e "console.log(require('@playwright/test').chromium.executablePath())")"
          echo "Using Chromium: $CHROME_PATH"
          test -x "$CHROME_PATH"

          npm run test:lighthouse

      - name: Upload Lighthouse reports
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: lighthouse-public-baseline-${{ github.sha }}
          path: artifacts/lighthouse-ci
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 30

  quality:
    needs:
      - plan
      - validation
      - browser
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 5

    steps:
      - name: Enforce required validation results
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
          PLAN_RESULT: ${{ needs.plan.result }}
          VALIDATION_REQUIRED: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.needsNpm }}
          VALIDATION_RESULT: ${{ needs.validation.result }}
          BROWSER_REQUIRED: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.e2e }}
          BROWSER_RESULT: ${{ needs.browser.result }}
          INTERMEDIATE_INGESTION_REQUIRED: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.intermediateIngestion }}
        run: |
          if [ "$PLAN_RESULT" != "success" ]; then
            echo "::error::Change planning did not complete successfully ($PLAN_RESULT)."
            exit 1
          fi

          if [ "$EVENT_NAME" != "push" ]; then
            if [ "$VALIDATION_REQUIRED" = "true" ] && [ "$VALIDATION_RESULT" != "success" ]; then
              echo "::error::Required validation did not complete successfully ($VALIDATION_RESULT)."
              exit 1
            fi

            if [ "$BROWSER_REQUIRED" = "true" ] && [ "$BROWSER_RESULT" != "success" ]; then
              echo "::error::Required browser validation did not complete successfully ($BROWSER_RESULT)."
              exit 1
            fi


            if [ "$INTERMEDIATE_INGESTION_REQUIRED" = "true" ]; then
              echo "Intermediate ingestion merge-gated acceptance passed through the existing validation and browser lanes."
            fi

            echo "Required change-aware Pull Request validation passed."
          else

            echo "Main push planning passed; full application quality was enforced before merge."
          fi

  deploy_frontend:
    needs:
      - plan
      - quality
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'push' &&
      github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' &&
      needs.plan.outputs.deployFrontend == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 20
    env:
      FRONTEND_URL: https://sport-analytics-tool-web.pages.dev
      CLOUDFLARE_PROJECT_NAME: sport-analytics-tool-web

    steps:
      - name: Check out validated main commit
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: package-lock.json

      - name: Install root workspace dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Validate deployment secrets
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          VITE_API_BASE_URL: ${{ secrets.VITE_API_BASE_URL }}
          VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY: ${{ secrets.VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY }}
          VITE_SUPABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.VITE_SUPABASE_URL }}
        run: |
          missing=0
          for name in CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID VITE_API_BASE_URL VITE_SUPABASE_URL VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY; do
            if [ -z "${!name}" ]; then
              echo "::error::Required Gitea secret $name is not configured."
              missing=1
            fi
          done
          exit "$missing"

      - name: Build shared contracts for deployment
        run: npm run build --workspace=@sport-analytics/contracts

      - name: Build frontend deployment bundle
        env:
          NODE_ENV: production
          VITE_API_BASE_URL: ${{ secrets.VITE_API_BASE_URL }}
          VITE_SUPABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.VITE_SUPABASE_URL }}
          VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY: ${{ secrets.VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY }}
        run: npm run build --workspace=@sport-analytics/frontend

      - name: Check bundle for embedded server-only secrets
        run: node scripts/check-frontend-bundle-secrets.mjs apps/frontend/dist

      - name: Deploy frontend to Cloudflare Pages
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
        run: npx wrangler pages deploy apps/frontend/dist --project-name=$CLOUDFLARE_PROJECT_NAME

      - name: Smoke check deployed frontend
        env:
          SMOKE_CHECK_ATTEMPTS: 18
          SMOKE_CHECK_DELAY_MS: 10000
          SMOKE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS: 15000
        run: >-
          node scripts/smoke-check-deployment.mjs
          "deployed frontend"
          "$FRONTEND_URL"
          "<title>Stat'sTheGame</title>"
  deploy_backend:
    needs:
      - plan
      - quality
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'push' &&
      github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' &&
      needs.plan.outputs.deployBackend == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 45
    env:
      ACR_NAME: statsthegamedevyhmqlinqfhkyg
      BACKEND_CONTAINER_APP_NAME: statsthegame-dev-api

    steps:
      - name: Check out validated main commit
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: package-lock.json

      - name: Install root workspace dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Validate Container Apps deployment configuration
        env:
          AZURE_WORKER_CREDENTIALS: ${{ secrets.AZURE_WORKER_CREDENTIALS }}
          AZURE_BACKEND_CONTAINER_RESOURCE_GROUP: ${{ secrets.AZURE_BACKEND_CONTAINER_RESOURCE_GROUP }}
          AZURE_BACKEND_DATABASE_SECRET_URI: ${{ secrets.AZURE_BACKEND_DATABASE_SECRET_URI }}
          AZURE_BACKEND_SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY_SECRET_URI: ${{ secrets.AZURE_BACKEND_SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY_SECRET_URI }}
          AZURE_BACKEND_ANONYMOUS_RATE_LIMIT_SECRET_URI: ${{ secrets.AZURE_BACKEND_ANONYMOUS_RATE_LIMIT_SECRET_URI }}
          AZURE_BACKEND_LLM_API_KEY_SECRET_URI: ${{ secrets.AZURE_BACKEND_LLM_API_KEY_SECRET_URI }}
          AZURE_BACKEND_CORS_ORIGINS: ${{ secrets.AZURE_BACKEND_CORS_ORIGINS }}
          AZURE_BACKEND_SUPABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.AZURE_BACKEND_SUPABASE_URL }}
          AZURE_BACKEND_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY: ${{ secrets.AZURE_BACKEND_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY }}
        run: |
          missing=0
          for name in AZURE_WORKER_CREDENTIALS AZURE_BACKEND_CONTAINER_RESOURCE_GROUP AZURE_BACKEND_DATABASE_SECRET_URI AZURE_BACKEND_SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY_SECRET_URI AZURE_BACKEND_ANONYMOUS_RATE_LIMIT_SECRET_URI AZURE_BACKEND_LLM_API_KEY_SECRET_URI AZURE_BACKEND_CORS_ORIGINS AZURE_BACKEND_SUPABASE_URL AZURE_BACKEND_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY; do
            if [ -z "${!name}" ]; then
              echo "::error::Required Gitea secret $name is not configured."
              missing=1
            fi
          done
          exit "$missing"

      - name: Verify Docker npm registry connectivity
        run: |
          echo "Checking DNS resolution inside Docker with the runner host network..."
          timeout 30s docker run --rm --network=host node:22-bookworm-slim \
            node -e "require('dns').lookup('registry.npmjs.org', (error, address) => { if (error) { console.error(error); process.exit(1); } console.log('registry.npmjs.org ->', address); })"

          echo "Checking npm registry connectivity inside Docker with the runner host network..."
          timeout 45s docker run --rm --network=host node:22-bookworm-slim \
            npm ping --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/

          echo "Docker npm registry connectivity verified."

      - name: Install Azure CLI
        run: |
          curl -sL https://aka.ms/InstallAzureCLIDeb | sudo bash
          az version

      - name: Sign in to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_WORKER_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Apply pending backend database migrations
        env:
          DATABASE_SECRET_URI: ${{ secrets.AZURE_BACKEND_DATABASE_SECRET_URI }}
        run: |
          echo "Applying reviewed backend database migrations before backend activation."
          DATABASE_URL="$(az keyvault secret show --id "$DATABASE_SECRET_URI" --query value --output tsv)"

          if [ -z "$DATABASE_URL" ]; then
            echo "::error::The backend database secret resolved to an empty value."
            exit 1
          fi

          export DATABASE_URL
          npm run db:migrate --workspace=@sport-analytics/backend

      - name: Sign in to Azure Container Registry
        run: az acr login --name "$ACR_NAME"

      - name: Prepare Docker Buildx
        run: |
          docker buildx version

          docker buildx rm -f backend-ci-builder >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

          docker buildx create \
            --name backend-ci-builder \
            --driver docker-container \
            --driver-opt network=host \
            --buildkitd-flags '--allow-insecure-entitlement network.host' \
            --use \
            --bootstrap

          docker buildx inspect

      - name: Verify Buildx npm registry connectivity
        shell: bash
        run: |
          timeout 60s docker buildx build \
            --progress=plain \
            --allow network.host \
            --network=host \
            --file - \
            . <<'EOF'
          FROM node:22-bookworm-slim
          RUN npm ping --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/
          EOF

      - name: Build immutable backend container image
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          build_log="$(mktemp)"
          trap 'rm -f "$build_log"' EXIT

            if ! docker buildx build \
              --progress=plain \
              --allow network.host \
              --network=host \
              --cache-from "type=registry,ref=$ACR_NAME.azurecr.io/sport-analytics-api:buildcache" \
              --cache-to "type=registry,ref=$ACR_NAME.azurecr.io/sport-analytics-api:buildcache,mode=max" \
              --file apps/backend/Dockerfile \
              --tag "$ACR_NAME.azurecr.io/sport-analytics-api:${{ github.sha }}" \
              --load \
              . 2>&1 | tee "$build_log"; then

            if grep -Fq 'Exit handler never called!' "$build_log"; then
              echo '::error::Backend Docker build failed: npm internal crash (Exit handler never called).'
            elif grep -Eqi 'EAI_AGAIN|ENOTFOUND|ECONNREFUSED|ECONNRESET|ETIMEDOUT|fetch failed' "$build_log"; then
              echo '::error::Backend Docker build failed: npm registry or Docker network failure.'
            elif grep -Eqi 'ELIFECYCLE|node-gyp|npm error (path|command|code [1-9][0-9]*)' "$build_log"; then
              echo '::error::Backend Docker build failed: lifecycle-script failure.'
            else
              echo '::error::Backend Docker build failed; inspect the BuildKit output above.'
            fi

            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Smoke check backend container image
        run: >-
          npm run smoke:backend-container --
          "$ACR_NAME.azurecr.io/sport-analytics-api:${{ github.sha }}"

      - name: Push immutable backend image to Azure Container Registry
        run: docker push "$ACR_NAME.azurecr.io/sport-analytics-api:${{ github.sha }}"

      - name: Deploy backend Container Apps revision
        env:
          RESOURCE_GROUP: ${{ secrets.AZURE_BACKEND_CONTAINER_RESOURCE_GROUP }}
          DATABASE_SECRET_URI: ${{ secrets.AZURE_BACKEND_DATABASE_SECRET_URI }}
          SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY_SECRET_URI: ${{ secrets.AZURE_BACKEND_SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY_SECRET_URI }}
          ANONYMOUS_RATE_LIMIT_SECRET_URI: ${{ secrets.AZURE_BACKEND_ANONYMOUS_RATE_LIMIT_SECRET_URI }}
          LLM_API_KEY_SECRET_URI: ${{ secrets.AZURE_BACKEND_LLM_API_KEY_SECRET_URI }}
          CORS_ORIGINS: ${{ secrets.AZURE_BACKEND_CORS_ORIGINS }}
          SUPABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.AZURE_BACKEND_SUPABASE_URL }}
          SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY: ${{ secrets.AZURE_BACKEND_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY }}
        run: >-
          az deployment group create
          --name backend-${{ github.sha }}
          --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP"
          --template-file infra/azure/backend/main.bicep
          --parameters
          containerImage="$ACR_NAME.azurecr.io/sport-analytics-api:${{ github.sha }}"
          databaseSecretUri="$DATABASE_SECRET_URI"
          supabaseSecretKeySecretUri="$SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY_SECRET_URI"
          anonymousRateLimitSecretUri="$ANONYMOUS_RATE_LIMIT_SECRET_URI"
          llmApiKeySecretUri="$LLM_API_KEY_SECRET_URI"
          corsOrigins="$CORS_ORIGINS"
          supabaseUrl="$SUPABASE_URL"
          supabasePublishableKey="$SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY"

      - name: Wait for the healthy backend Container Apps revision
        env:
          RESOURCE_GROUP: ${{ secrets.AZURE_BACKEND_CONTAINER_RESOURCE_GROUP }}
        run: |
          EXPECTED_IMAGE="$ACR_NAME.azurecr.io/sport-analytics-api:${{ github.sha }}"

          for attempt in {1..12}; do
            MATCHING_REVISION=$(az containerapp revision list \
              --name "$BACKEND_CONTAINER_APP_NAME" \
              --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" \
              --query "[?properties.active && properties.healthState=='Healthy' && properties.template.containers[0].image=='$EXPECTED_IMAGE'] | [0].name" \
              -o tsv)

            echo "Backend revision readiness check $attempt/12"

            az containerapp revision list \
              --name "$BACKEND_CONTAINER_APP_NAME" \
              --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" \
              --query "[?properties.active].{Revision:name,Health:properties.healthState,Image:properties.template.containers[0].image}" \
              -o table

            if [ -n "$MATCHING_REVISION" ]; then
              echo "Verified healthy backend revision: $MATCHING_REVISION"
              exit 0
            fi

            sleep 10
          done

          echo "::error::Expected backend image $EXPECTED_IMAGE did not become active and healthy within 120 seconds."
          exit 1

      - name: Resolve backend Container Apps HTTPS endpoint
        env:
          RESOURCE_GROUP: ${{ secrets.AZURE_BACKEND_CONTAINER_RESOURCE_GROUP }}
        run: |
          BACKEND_FQDN=$(az containerapp show \
            --name "$BACKEND_CONTAINER_APP_NAME" \
            --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" \
            --query properties.configuration.ingress.fqdn \
            -o tsv)

          if [ -z "$BACKEND_FQDN" ]; then
            echo "::error::Backend Container App has no external ingress FQDN."
            exit 1
          fi

          echo "BACKEND_URL=https://$BACKEND_FQDN" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Smoke check deployed backend health
        env:
          SMOKE_CHECK_ATTEMPTS: 18
          SMOKE_CHECK_DELAY_MS: 10000
          SMOKE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS: 15000
        run: >-
          node scripts/smoke-check-deployment.mjs
          "deployed backend health"
          "$BACKEND_URL/api/v1/health"
          "sport-analytics-api"

      - name: Smoke check deployed database access
        env:
          SMOKE_CHECK_ATTEMPTS: 6
          SMOKE_CHECK_DELAY_MS: 5000
          SMOKE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS: 15000
        run: >-
          node scripts/smoke-check-deployment.mjs
          "deployed backend database access"
          "$BACKEND_URL/api/v1/competitions?limit=1"
          "pagination"

      - name: Smoke check deployed dataset-release schema access
        env:
          SMOKE_CHECK_ATTEMPTS: 6
          SMOKE_CHECK_DELAY_MS: 5000
          SMOKE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS: 15000
        run: >-
          node scripts/smoke-check-deployment.mjs
          "deployed dataset-release schema access"
          "$BACKEND_URL/api/v1/dataset-releases"
          "data"

  deploy_docs:
    needs:
      - plan
      - quality
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'push' &&
      github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' &&
      needs.plan.outputs.deployDocs == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 20
    env:
      DOCS_URL: https://sports-analytics-tool.pages.dev
      CLOUDFLARE_PROJECT_NAME: sports-analytics-tool

    steps:
      - name: Check out validated main commit
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Validate deployment secrets
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "$CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN" ]; then
            echo "::error::Required Gitea secret CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN is not configured."
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ -z "$CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID" ]; then
            echo "::error::Required Gitea secret CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID is not configured."
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: package-lock.json

      - name: Install root workspace dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'
          cache: pip
          cache-dependency-path: requirements-docs.txt

      - name: Install documentation dependencies
        run: python -m pip install -r requirements-docs.txt

      - name: Build documentation strictly
        run: python -m mkdocs build --strict

      - name: Deploy documentation to Cloudflare Pages
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
        run: npx wrangler pages deploy site --project-name=$CLOUDFLARE_PROJECT_NAME

      - name: Smoke check deployed documentation site
        env:
          SMOKE_CHECK_ATTEMPTS: 12
          SMOKE_CHECK_DELAY_MS: 10000
          SMOKE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS: 15000
        run: >-
          node scripts/smoke-check-deployment.mjs
          "deployed documentation site"
          "$DOCS_URL/"
          "Sport Analytics Tool"
  deploy_worker:
    needs:
      - plan
      - quality
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'push' &&
      github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' &&
      needs.plan.outputs.deployWorker == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 45

    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: package-lock.json

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Verify worker
        run: |
          npm run lint --workspace=@sport-analytics/worker
          npm run typecheck --workspace=@sport-analytics/worker
          npm run test --workspace=@sport-analytics/worker
          npm run build --workspace=@sport-analytics/worker

      - name: Validate deployment secrets
        env:
          AZURE_WORKER_CREDENTIALS: ${{ secrets.AZURE_WORKER_CREDENTIALS }}
          AZURE_WORKER_RESOURCE_GROUP: ${{ secrets.AZURE_WORKER_RESOURCE_GROUP }}
          AZURE_WORKER_KEY_VAULT_NAME: ${{ secrets.AZURE_WORKER_KEY_VAULT_NAME }}
          AZURE_WORKER_DATABASE_SECRET_URI: ${{ secrets.AZURE_WORKER_DATABASE_SECRET_URI }}
        run: |
          missing=0
          for name in AZURE_WORKER_CREDENTIALS AZURE_WORKER_RESOURCE_GROUP AZURE_WORKER_KEY_VAULT_NAME AZURE_WORKER_DATABASE_SECRET_URI; do
            if [ -z "${!name}" ]; then
              echo "::error::Required Gitea secret $name is not configured."
              missing=1
            fi
          done
          exit "$missing"

      - name: Install Azure CLI
        run: |
          curl -sL https://aka.ms/InstallAzureCLIDeb | sudo bash
          az version

      - name: Sign in to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_WORKER_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Provision worker infrastructure
        env:
          RESOURCE_GROUP: ${{ secrets.AZURE_WORKER_RESOURCE_GROUP }}
          KEY_VAULT_NAME: ${{ secrets.AZURE_WORKER_KEY_VAULT_NAME }}
          DATABASE_SECRET_URI: ${{ secrets.AZURE_WORKER_DATABASE_SECRET_URI }}
        run: >-
          az deployment group create
          --name worker-${{ github.sha }}-infra
          --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP"
          --template-file infra/azure/worker/main.bicep
          --parameters deployWorker=false minReplicas=1
          keyVaultName="$KEY_VAULT_NAME"
          databaseSecretUri="$DATABASE_SECRET_URI"
          storageAccountName=statsthegameblobdev

      - name: Verify Docker npm registry connectivity
        run: |
          MAX_CONNECTIVITY_ATTEMPTS=4
          CONNECTIVITY_RETRY_BASE_SECONDS=5

          for attempt in $(seq 1 "$MAX_CONNECTIVITY_ATTEMPTS"); do
            echo "Docker npm registry connectivity attempt $attempt/$MAX_CONNECTIVITY_ATTEMPTS"

            echo "Checking DNS resolution inside Docker..."
            if ! docker run --rm --network=host node:22-bookworm-slim \
              node -e "require('dns').lookup('registry.npmjs.org', (error, address) => { if (error) { console.error(error); process.exit(1); } console.log('registry.npmjs.org ->', address); })"; then
              failure_stage="DNS resolution"
            else
              echo "Checking npm registry connectivity inside Docker..."
              if docker run --rm --network=host node:22-bookworm-slim \
                npm ping --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/; then
                echo "Docker npm registry connectivity verified."
                exit 0
              fi
              failure_stage="npm registry connectivity"
            fi

            if [ "$attempt" -eq "$MAX_CONNECTIVITY_ATTEMPTS" ]; then
              echo "::error::Docker npm registry connectivity failed after $MAX_CONNECTIVITY_ATTEMPTS attempts; last failure: $failure_stage."
              exit 1
            fi

            retry_delay=$((CONNECTIVITY_RETRY_BASE_SECONDS * (2 ** (attempt - 1))))
            echo "::warning::Docker npm registry connectivity attempt $attempt/$MAX_CONNECTIVITY_ATTEMPTS failed during $failure_stage; retrying in ${retry_delay}s."
            sleep "$retry_delay"
          done

      - name: Build immutable worker image and push to Azure Container Registry
        env:
          RESOURCE_GROUP: ${{ secrets.AZURE_WORKER_RESOURCE_GROUP }}
        run: |
          INFRA_DEPLOYMENT_NAME="worker-${{ github.sha }}-infra"

          ACR_NAME=$(az deployment group show \
            --name "$INFRA_DEPLOYMENT_NAME" \
            --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" \
            --query properties.outputs.containerRegistryName.value \
            -o tsv)

          ACR_SERVER=$(az deployment group show \
            --name "$INFRA_DEPLOYMENT_NAME" \
            --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" \
            --query properties.outputs.containerRegistryServer.value \
            -o tsv)

          echo "Building worker image for registry $ACR_NAME"

          az acr login --name "$ACR_NAME"

          docker pull "$ACR_SERVER/sport-analytics-worker:buildcache" || true

          DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 docker build \
            --network=host \
            --file apps/worker/Dockerfile \
            --build-arg BUILDKIT_INLINE_CACHE=1 \
            --cache-from "$ACR_SERVER/sport-analytics-worker:buildcache" \
            --tag "$ACR_SERVER/sport-analytics-worker:${{ github.sha }}" \
            --tag "$ACR_SERVER/sport-analytics-worker:buildcache" \
            .

          docker push "$ACR_SERVER/sport-analytics-worker:${{ github.sha }}"
          docker push "$ACR_SERVER/sport-analytics-worker:buildcache"

          echo "ACR_NAME=$ACR_NAME" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "ACR_SERVER=$ACR_SERVER" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Deploy worker revision
        env:
          RESOURCE_GROUP: ${{ secrets.AZURE_WORKER_RESOURCE_GROUP }}
          KEY_VAULT_NAME: ${{ secrets.AZURE_WORKER_KEY_VAULT_NAME }}
          DATABASE_SECRET_URI: ${{ secrets.AZURE_WORKER_DATABASE_SECRET_URI }}
        run: >-
          az deployment group create
          --name worker-${{ github.sha }}
          --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP"
          --template-file infra/azure/worker/main.bicep
          --parameters deployWorker=true minReplicas=1
          containerImage="$ACR_NAME.azurecr.io/sport-analytics-worker:${{ github.sha }}"
          keyVaultName="$KEY_VAULT_NAME"
          databaseSecretUri="$DATABASE_SECRET_URI"
          storageAccountName=statsthegameblobdev

      - name: Verify active revision image and health
        env:
          RESOURCE_GROUP: ${{ secrets.AZURE_WORKER_RESOURCE_GROUP }}
        run: |
          EXPECTED_IMAGE="$ACR_SERVER/sport-analytics-worker:${{ github.sha }}"
          LIVE_MIN_REPLICAS=$(az containerapp show \
            --name statsthegame-dev-batch-worker \
            --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" \
            --query 'properties.template.scale.minReplicas' \
            -o tsv)

          if [ "$LIVE_MIN_REPLICAS" != "1" ]; then
            echo "::error::Worker minimum replicas is $LIVE_MIN_REPLICAS; expected 1."
            exit 1
          fi

          echo "Expected worker image: $EXPECTED_IMAGE"
          echo "Verified worker minimum replicas: $LIVE_MIN_REPLICAS"

          for attempt in {1..12}; do
            MATCHING_REVISION=$(az containerapp revision list \
              --name statsthegame-dev-batch-worker \
              --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" \
              --query "[?properties.active && properties.healthState=='Healthy' && properties.template.containers[0].image=='$EXPECTED_IMAGE'] | [0].name" \
              -o tsv)

            echo "Worker verification $attempt/12"

            az containerapp revision list \
              --name statsthegame-dev-batch-worker \
              --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" \
              --query "[?properties.active].{Revision:name,Health:properties.healthState,Image:properties.template.containers[0].image}" \
              -o table

            if [ -n "$MATCHING_REVISION" ]; then
              echo "Verified healthy active worker revision: $MATCHING_REVISION"
              echo "Verified worker image: $EXPECTED_IMAGE"
              exit 0
            fi

            sleep 10
          done

          echo "::error::Expected worker image $EXPECTED_IMAGE did not become active and healthy within 120 seconds."
          exit 1

  coverage:
    needs:
      - plan
      - quality
      - deploy_frontend
      - deploy_backend
      - deploy_docs
      - deploy_worker
    if: >-
      always() &&
      needs.plan.outputs.coverage == 'true' &&
      needs.quality.result == 'success'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: write
    env:
      NODE_ENV: test
      SUPABASE_URL: https://example.invalid
      SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY: test-publishable-key
      COVERAGE_THRESHOLD_LINES: ${{ vars.COVERAGE_THRESHOLD_LINES }}
      COVERAGE_THRESHOLD_STATEMENTS: ${{ vars.COVERAGE_THRESHOLD_STATEMENTS }}
      COVERAGE_THRESHOLD_FUNCTIONS: ${{ vars.COVERAGE_THRESHOLD_FUNCTIONS }}
      COVERAGE_THRESHOLD_BRANCHES: ${{ vars.COVERAGE_THRESHOLD_BRANCHES }}

    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: package-lock.json

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Generate repository-wide coverage
        id: repository_coverage
        shell: bash
        run: |
          mkdir -p coverage
          set +e
          npm run test:coverage
          coverage_exit_code=$?
          set -e

          echo "exit_code=$coverage_exit_code" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

          if [ "$coverage_exit_code" -eq 0 ]; then
            printf 'Coverage: PASS\n' > coverage/ci-status.txt
            echo "Repository coverage completed successfully."
          else
            printf 'Coverage: FAILED / INCOMPLETE\nExit code: %s\n' "$coverage_exit_code" > coverage/ci-status.txt
            echo "::warning::Coverage FAILED / INCOMPLETE (exit code $coverage_exit_code). Quality and deployment have already completed; retaining this as non-blocking evidence."
          fi

          # Coverage is a late evidence signal. Preserve the real exit code as
          # output/status evidence without turning it back into a deployment gate.
          exit 0

      - name: Upload repository coverage reports
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: repository-coverage-${{ github.sha }}
          path: coverage/
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 14

      - name: Publish live coverage badge
        if: steps.repository_coverage.outputs.exit_code == '0' && github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cp coverage/combined/badge.svg "$RUNNER_TEMP/coverage-badge.svg"

          git config user.name "gitea-actions"
          git config user.email "actions@users.noreply.sdp.ms.wits.ac.za"

          git fetch origin coverage-badge || true
          if git show-ref --verify --quiet refs/remotes/origin/coverage-badge; then
            git switch -C coverage-badge origin/coverage-badge
          else
            git switch --orphan coverage-badge
            git rm -rf . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
          fi

          cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/coverage-badge.svg" badge.svg
          git add badge.svg
          if git diff --cached --quiet; then
            echo "Coverage badge is already current."
            exit 0
          fi

          git commit -m "chore(coverage): update live badge"
          git push origin coverage-badge

      - name: Report repository coverage status
        if: always()
        shell: bash
        run: |
          if [ "${{ steps.repository_coverage.outputs.exit_code }}" = "0" ]; then
            echo "Repository coverage evidence completed successfully."
          else
            echo "::warning::Repository coverage FAILED / INCOMPLETE. This late evidence signal did not gate quality or deployment."
          fi

# Repository scripts

The `scripts/` directory contains developer-facing repository automation and data-support utilities. Run scripts from the repository root unless a script's specialist documentation says otherwise.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 20 or later and npm 10 or later for `.mjs` scripts and root npm commands;
- Python 3.10 or later for `.py` data utilities;
- Docker Desktop or a compatible Docker Compose runtime only for `test-database-local.mjs`; and
- internet access for the Cricsheet downloader and deployed-service smoke checks where applicable.

Install the committed JavaScript dependency graph first:

```bash
npm ci
```

## Developer-facing Node.js scripts

| Script                              | Normal entry point                                                                          | Purpose / safe usage                                                                                                                            |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `run-development-app.mjs`           | `npm run dev`, `npm run dev:frontend`, `npm run dev:backend`                                | Dispatches the selected workspace development server.                                                                                           |
| `check-required-files.mjs`          | `npm run structure:check`                                                                   | Verifies repository files required by the project structure and onboarding rules.                                                               |
| `verify-intermediate-ingestion.mjs` | `npm run verify:intermediate-ingestion`; `npm run verify:intermediate-ingestion:invariants` | Runs Issue #364's retained full local acceptance exercise, or only the unique evidence/log-safety invariants reused by change-aware CI.         |
| `test-database-local.mjs`           | `npm run test:database:local`                                                               | Starts the isolated Docker PostgreSQL 16 test environment and runs database integration tests. Never repoint it at development/production data. |
| `prepare-backend-deployment.mjs`    | `npm run deploy:prepare:backend`                                                            | Builds the backend deployment artifact used by the Azure workflow. Generated deployment output is not source code.                              |
| `deploy-backend-azure.py`           | automatic/manual backend deployment                                                         | Creates the prepared backend ZIP and performs the shared Azure Kudu deployment/status logic after quality validation.                           |
| `smoke-check-backend-artifact.mjs`  | deployment workflow/helper use                                                              | Checks the prepared backend artifact locally before deployment.                                                                                 |
| `smoke-check-deployment.mjs`        | deployment workflow/helper use                                                              | Performs retrying content-aware HTTP checks against deployed services. Use only against the intended documented target.                         |

## Cricsheet and data-support Python scripts

| Script                          | Purpose                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `download_cricsheet_t20.py`     | Downloads the scoped Cricsheet T20/IT20 source corpus. Generated data is ignored by Git. |
| `catalogue_cricsheet_fields.py` | Catalogues fields observed in the downloaded Cricsheet source data.                      |
| `probe_cricsheet_edge_cases.py` | Investigates source-data edge cases used in schema/design work.                          |
| `probe_delivery_over_key.py`    | Probes delivery/over key behaviour in source data.                                       |
| `probe_match_metadata.py`       | Inspects match metadata patterns in source data.                                         |
| `find_miscounted.py`            | Investigates source/statistic counting anomalies.                                        |
| `find_super_overs.py`           | Locates and inspects super-over cases.                                                   |
| `make_invalid_seeds.py`         | Produces intentionally invalid seed fixtures for validation work.                        |
| `validate_source_totals.py`     | Cross-checks source totals used during data validation.                                  |

The main acquisition command is:

```bash
python scripts/download_cricsheet_t20.py
```

Use the probe/validation utilities only when their input data is present and you understand what they read or generate. Do not commit downloaded bulk datasets, temporary probe output or generated files unless a related issue explicitly requires a sanitized evidence artefact.

## Gitea export helper

The `scripts/gitea-export/` subdirectory has its own [Gitea export helper guide](gitea-export/README.md). Follow that guide for project-board and issue export work rather than duplicating its setup here.

    const workflow = readFileSync(workflowPath, 'utf8');

    const buildStart = workflow.indexOf(

      probeStart,

      -1,
      `${workflowPath} must retain the Docker npm connectivity guard`,

    );

# AI usage registers

Each team member records their AI usage in their own file under `registers/`.
The file is named to match the member''s transcript folder under `transcripts/`.

The single shared register at `ai-usage-register.csv` is being retired. It was
edited by all six members, conflicted on almost every merge, and was corrupted
three times. Entries remain in both files until every member has created their
own, after which the shared register is removed.

## Columns

| Column                     | Content                                                            |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Date                       | The date the work was done, as `YYYY-MM-DD`.                       |
| Team member                | The member who used the tool.                                      |
| Tool                       | The tool used, for example `Claude Web` or `ChatGPT Web`.          |
| Model                      | The model used, for example `Claude Opus 5` or `GPT-5.6 Thinking`. |
| Purpose                    | The kinds of use, separated by semicolons.                         |
| Brief task                 | What the work was, including the issue number where applicable.    |
| Output used                | What was produced and actually used.                               |
| Verification or adaptation | How the output was checked, tested or changed before use.          |
| Related evidence           | Transcript paths, issue numbers and Pull Requests.                 |

## Rules

Every field must be quoted, including the date. Fields contain commas and
semicolons, and an unquoted field containing a comma breaks the file for every
reader.

Every file must end with a trailing newline. A row appended to a file without one
is fused onto the row above it.

Use a semicolon, not a comma, to separate items within a field.

Only tools and models genuinely used may be listed. The register is a record of
what happened, not a declaration of what was permitted.

## Relationship to other attribution

This register does not replace the attribution the course AI policy requires
elsewhere. Commits containing AI-generated code carry an `Assisted-by` line,
documents carry an AI declaration, and the repository README declares the tools
in use.

FILE: docs/git-methodology.md
# Git Methodology

| Document Information | Details                       |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| Project              | Sport Analytics Tool          |
| Platform             | Gitea                         |
| Methodology          | GitHub Flow adapted for Gitea |
| Document Version     | 1.0                           |
| Date                 | 4 August 2026                 |
| Status               | Approved for Use              |
| Team                 | Git Push Pray                 |

## 1. Purpose

This document defines the Git methodology that will be followed throughout the development of the Sport Analytics Tool.

The methodology establishes:

- when commits must be created;
- how commit messages must be written;
- when branches must be created;
- how branches must be named;
- when branches may be merged;
- the requirements that must be met before merging;
- when project versions must be created; and
- how project versions must be named.

The purpose of the methodology is to maintain an organised repository, support effective collaboration, reduce merge conflicts, enable code review and provide traceability between requirements and their implementation.

All team members are required to apply this methodology consistently across all project repositories.

## 2. Selected Methodology

The team will use **GitHub Flow adapted for Gitea**.

Under this methodology:

1. `main` contains the latest reviewed and working version of the project.
2. Each significant unit of work begins as a Gitea issue.
3. A short-lived branch is created for the issue.
4. Development is completed through small, meaningful commits.
5. The branch, commits and Pull Request reference the issue.
6. A Pull Request is reviewed before it is merged.
7. Approved work is merged into `main`.
8. Important milestone states are identified using Git tags.

This methodology was selected because it provides sufficient control, traceability and peer review without introducing unnecessary permanent branches or administrative processes.

A more complex methodology, such as Git Flow, would require additional `develop`, `release` and `hotfix` branches. These branches are not necessary for the size, duration or release structure of this project.

The selected methodology is therefore intended to remain lightweight enough to be followed consistently by all team members.

## 3. The `main` Branch

The `main` branch represents the latest integrated, reviewed and working version of the project.

The following rules apply to `main`:

- Direct development on `main` is prohibited.
- Direct pushes to `main` are prohibited.
- Changes may only enter `main` through an approved Gitea Pull Request.
- `main` must remain in a buildable and working state.
- Force pushes to `main` are prohibited.
- Required automated checks must pass before a Pull Request may be merged.
- A Pull Request must be up to date with `main` before merge so the required status represents the
  integration state that will enter `main`.
- Milestone version tags may only be created from `main`.

The `main` branch will be protected using Giteaâ€™s branch-protection settings where these settings are available.
The protection should require `Sport Analytics CI / quality (pull_request)` and block merging an
out-of-date Pull Request. These protections are particularly important because post-merge CI performs
deployment-specific work instead of repeating the complete Pull Request application suite.

## 4. Gitea Issues and Traceability

Every significant development task must begin as a Gitea issue.

An issue must contain:

- a clear title;
- a description of the required work;
- acceptance criteria;
- an assigned team member;
- the relevant sprint milestone; and
- appropriate labels.

Examples of work that requires an issue include:

- implementing a feature;
- fixing a bug;
- creating or changing an API endpoint;
- changing the database schema;
- adding automated tests;
- configuring infrastructure or CI/CD;
- completing substantial documentation; and
- performing a technical investigation that will influence development.

Very small corrections, such as correcting a spelling error, may be included in an existing relevant issue.

Each significant change will remain traceable from its Gitea issue through the branches,
commits and Pull Requests used to implement it.

A small issue will normally follow:

Gitea issue â†’ branch â†’ commits â†’ Pull Request â†’ merge

A larger issue may be implemented through multiple reviewable Pull Requests:

Gitea issue
â”œâ”€â”€ branch â†’ commits â†’ Pull Request â†’ merge
â””â”€â”€ branch â†’ commits â†’ Pull Request â†’ merge

In that case, each Pull Request must reference the same parent issue, and the issue remains open
until all acceptance criteria have been satisfied.
For example, work related to issue `#12` would be recorded as follows:

```text
Issue:        #12 Validate event submissions
Branch:       feat/12-validate-event-submissions
Commit body:  Refs #12
Pull Request: #12 Validate event submissions
PR body:      Closes #12
```

This process allows the team to trace completed work back to its original requirement, implementation, review and final integration.

## 5. When to Create a Branch

A branch must be created when a team member begins work on a Gitea issue involving code, tests, configuration or substantial documentation.

Before creating a branch:

1. The related Gitea issue must exist.
2. The issue must have a clear description.
3. The issue must contain acceptance criteria.
4. The issue must have an assignee.
5. The issue must be assigned to the relevant sprint milestone.
6. The developer must update their local copy of `main`.

The branch must be created from the latest version of `main`.

```bash
git switch main
git pull origin main
git switch -c feat/12-validate-event-submissions
```

A branch should normally address one Gitea issue.

Where two issues cannot reasonably be separated, both issue numbers must be identified in the Pull Request description.

Branches must be short-lived. A normal branch should be completed within five working days. A branch may not remain open beyond the sprint in which it was created unless the delay and reason are recorded in the related issue.

If a branch becomes too large to review effectively, the work should be divided into smaller
reviewable branches and Pull Requests. Where those parts represent independently trackable work,
separate child or follow-up issues may also be created.

## 6. How to Name Branches

Branch names must follow this format:

```text
<type>/<issue-number>-<short-description>
```

The approved branch types are:

| Type       | Purpose                                          |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `feat`     | New functionality                                |
| `fix`      | Correction of incorrect behaviour                |
| `docs`     | Documentation changes                            |
| `test`     | Test creation or modification                    |
| `refactor` | Code restructuring without a change in behaviour |
| `chore`    | Maintenance, setup or configuration              |
| `ci`       | Continuous integration or deployment changes     |

Examples include:

```text
feat/12-validate-event-submissions
fix/18-prevent-duplicate-statistics
docs/21-add-api-documentation
test/24-test-event-validation
refactor/31-extract-statistics-service
chore/7-configure-project
ci/9-add-backend-pipeline
```

Branch names must:

- use lowercase letters;
- contain the related issue number;
- separate words using hyphens;
- contain no spaces;
- use a concise but meaningful description; and
- reflect the main purpose of the branch.

## 7. When to Commit

A commit must be created whenever one small, logically complete unit of work has been completed.

Each commit must:

- represent one identifiable change;
- relate to the issue assigned to the branch;
- leave the affected section of the project in a working state;
- not knowingly introduce compilation or build failures;
- not knowingly cause existing tests to fail;
- exclude unrelated changes; and
- be understandable independently of later commits.

Examples of suitable commits include:

- creating the fixture database model;
- adding event-schema validation;
- implementing one API endpoint;
- correcting one calculation error;
- adding tests for one endpoint;
- updating the setup instructions for one service.

A commit must not combine unrelated work. For example, a single commit should not contain an unrelated API feature, user-interface redesign and documentation rewrite.

Developers must commit regularly and must not wait until an entire sprint or large feature has been completed before creating a commit.

Temporary commits may be used while work is in progress. However, commits with unclear messages such as `WIP`, `fix stuff` or `more changes` must not remain in a branch submitted for final review.

## 8. How to Write Commit Messages

The team will use a simplified Conventional Commit format.

The required format is:

```text
<type>(<scope>): <description>
```

The scope may be omitted when it does not provide useful additional information:

```text
<type>: <description>
```

### 8.1 Approved Commit Types

| Type       | Purpose                                           |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `feat`     | Adds new functionality                            |
| `fix`      | Corrects incorrect behaviour                      |
| `docs`     | Changes documentation only                        |
| `test`     | Adds or modifies tests                            |
| `refactor` | Restructures code without changing behaviour      |
| `chore`    | Changes maintenance, setup or configuration files |
| `ci`       | Changes the CI/CD process                         |

### 8.2 Commit Message Requirements

The commit description must:

- begin with a lowercase verb;
- state what the commit accomplishes;
- be concise but specific;
- use the imperative form; and
- avoid vague descriptions.

Acceptable commit messages include:

```text
feat(api): add event submission endpoint
fix(stats): prevent duplicate events from affecting totals
test(api): add invalid event submission cases
docs(setup): document local database configuration
ci: run backend tests on pull requests
```

Unacceptable commit messages include:

```text
updated files
fixed things
more work
changes
final version
stuff
```

### 8.3 Linking Commits to Issues

Every normal development commit must reference the related Gitea issue in its commit body.

```text
feat(api): validate submitted event structure

Refs #12
```

The issue will normally be closed by the Pull Request rather than by an individual commit. This ensures that the issue remains open until all associated work has been reviewed and merged.

Merge commits, automated dependency commits and automatically generated revert commits are exempt from the normal issue-reference requirement where a manual reference would not be appropriate.

### 8.4 AI-Assisted Code

Where AI-generated code is included in a commit, the commit body must include the required tool and model attribution.

```text
feat(api): validate submitted event structure

Refs #12
Assisted-by: ChatGPT-Web[GPT-5.6 Thinking]
```

Only tools and models genuinely used in producing the code contained in that commit may be listed.

---

## 9. When to Open a Pull Request

A Pull Request must be opened when the work on a branch is ready for review.

Before opening a Pull Request, the author must:

1. review the changes personally;
2. update the branch with the latest version of `main`;
3. resolve all merge conflicts;
4. run the relevant tests locally;
5. remove debugging code and unnecessary temporary files;
6. confirm that the issueâ€™s acceptance criteria have been addressed;
7. update relevant documentation;
8. confirm that no credentials or sensitive information have been committed; and
9. include the required AI attribution where applicable.

A draft Pull Request may be opened earlier when feedback is required before the work is complete. A draft Pull Request must be clearly identified and may not be merged.

The Pull Request title must contain the related issue number:

```text
#12 Validate event submissions
```

The Pull Request description must include:

```markdown
## Purpose

Explain why the change is required.

## Changes

Summarise the main changes made.

## Testing

Explain how the change was tested.

## Known Limitations

List any remaining limitations, or state that none are known.

## Related Issue

Closes #12
```

Where the Pull Request represents only part of a larger issue, use:

```markdown
## Related Issue

Refs #12
```

`Closes #<issue-number>` should only be used where that Pull Request completes the issue.
Where additional Pull Requests are still required, use `Refs #<issue-number>` so that the
parent issue remains open.

## 10. When to Merge

A branch may only be merged after its Pull Request has completed the required review and verification process.

A developer may not merge their own Pull Request without approval from at least one other team member.

The team will use **merge commits** when merging Pull Requests into `main`.

Merge commits were selected because they preserve:

- the individual development commits;
- the identity of the feature branch;
- the Pull Request as a distinct unit of work; and
- the relationship between the issue and its implementation.

After a Pull Request has been merged:

1. The related Gitea issue must be closed if the merged Pull Request satisfies all remaining
   acceptance criteria. If the issue requires additional Pull Requests, it remains open until the
   complete issue scope is finished.
2. The completed branch must be deleted from Gitea.
3. The associated Project board item must be moved to `Done` only when the parent issue is complete.
4. Any incomplete or follow-up work outside the parent issue's acceptance criteria must be recorded
   as a new issue.

## 11. Requirements for Merging

A Pull Request may be merged only when all the following requirements have been satisfied.

### 11.1 Issue and Scope

- The Pull Request is linked to at least one Gitea issue.
- The issueâ€™s acceptance criteria have been met.
- The Pull Request contains no unrelated changes.
- Any approved change in scope has been recorded in the issue.

### 11.2 Description

- The purpose of the change is explained.
- The main implementation changes are summarised.
- The testing process is described.
- Known limitations are documented.
- The related issue is identified using `Closes #<issue-number>` when the Pull Request completes
  the issue, or `Refs #<issue-number>` when additional Pull Requests remain.

### 11.3 Review

- The author has reviewed their own changes.
- At least one team member other than the author has reviewed the Pull Request.
- At least one approval has been recorded.
- All reviewer comments have been answered.
- All requested changes have been implemented or formally resolved.
- The reviewer has confirmed that the implementation matches its stated purpose.

### 11.4 Testing and Quality

- All relevant automated tests pass.
- Existing tests continue to pass.
- All required CI checks pass.
- Formatting, linting and type-checking checks pass where configured.
- The affected application or service builds successfully.
- Deployment checks pass where the change affects deployment.
- No unresolved merge conflicts remain.
- No credentials, secrets or sensitive information are included.
- No unnecessary generated or temporary files are included.

### 11.5 Documentation

- Relevant technical documentation has been updated.
- Setup instructions have been updated where necessary.
- API documentation has been updated where an endpoint or schema changed.
- Database documentation has been updated where the schema changed.
- AI assistance has been declared where required.

A Pull Request that does not meet every applicable requirement must not be merged.

## 12. When to Create a Version

A project version will be created when the team reaches a formal assessed milestone and the corresponding code has been reviewed and stabilised.

Versions will be created for:

- Sprint 1;
- Sprint 2;
- Sprint 3; and
- the final submission.

A version may only be created when:

1. All work included in the milestone has been merged into `main`.
2. The milestone version builds successfully.
3. All required automated checks pass.
4. The team has reviewed the milestone state.
5. Known defects and limitations have been documented.
6. The exact commit being submitted has been confirmed.
7. The repository documentation accurately reflects the submitted state.

The version will be recorded using an annotated Git tag created from `main`.

## 13. How to Name Versions

The project will use descriptive milestone versioning.

The primary version tags will be:

```text
sprint-1
sprint-2
sprint-3
final-submission
```

If an authorised correction is required after a milestone version has been created, the corrected version will use a numbered revision:

```text
sprint-1.1
sprint-1.2
```

An existing tag may not be moved, renamed or overwritten. A new tag must be created so that the original submitted version remains available.

Descriptive milestone versioning was selected because the projectâ€™s most significant development versions correspond directly with its assessed milestones. This makes versions clear to both the development team and project assessors.

## 14. Standard Development Workflow

All significant work must follow the process below:

1. Create a Gitea issue.
2. Add a description and acceptance criteria.
3. Assign the issue to a team member and sprint milestone.
4. Update the local `main` branch.
5. Create a branch containing the issue number.
6. Complete the work using small, atomic commits.
7. Reference the issue in each applicable commit.
8. Test and review the work locally.
9. Open a Pull Request linked to the issue.
10. Obtain approval from another team member.
11. Resolve all review comments.
12. Ensure all required checks pass.
13. Merge the Pull Request into `main` using a merge commit.
14. Close the issue once all Pull Requests required to satisfy its acceptance criteria have been merged.
15. Delete the completed branch.
16. Move the Project board item to `Done` once the issue is complete.
17. Create a version tag when the relevant milestone is complete.

## 15. Methodology Review and Change Control

This methodology is intended to remain in use for the duration of the project.

The team will not change the methodology merely because another process appears more convenient or because individual team members prefer a different workflow. Consistent use is necessary to maintain an understandable repository history and provide reliable evidence of the teamâ€™s development process.

The methodology may only be changed where there is clear evidence that the current process is causing significant or repeated problems. Examples include:

- repeated merge conflicts caused by the workflow;
- substantial delays in reviewing or integrating work;
- a Gitea limitation that prevents the methodology from being followed;
- a process requirement that creates unnecessary work without providing value;
- difficulty tracing issues to their implementation; or
- a project change that makes the existing methodology unsuitable.

Before changing the methodology:

1. The problem must be discussed by the full team.
2. Evidence of the problem must be identified.
3. The proposed change and its expected benefit must be explained.
4. The change must be approved by a majority of the team.
